title: More Space for Your Child: How Do We Grant Them Trust and Responsibility?
summary:
Do you sometimes find yourself wondering: When did my child get so big? Time flies, and here your child is, 10-12 years old, no longer that little one who needs your hand every step of the way. Perhaps you notice they prefer to spend some time alone, or express a strong opinion in their choices, or even complain about your excessive interference. These are completely natural signs that they are preparing for a new stage of independence, and it's a wonderful opportunity to boost their self-confidence and capabilities.

The essence of this stage lies in the gentle shift from the role of controller to the role of supervisor and supporter. Your child no longer needs someone to decide everything for them, but rather someone to guide them and give them space to learn from their experiences. Responsibility is not a burden; it is the fuel for maturity. When we give our children real tasks that suit their abilities, such as managing their own allowance, organizing their study schedule, or even contributing with specific household chores, we build in them a sense of competence and self-reliance.

Start with small, calculated steps. Choose one responsibility your child can handle now, and present it to them with confidence, emphasizing that you will be there for support and help when needed. Allow them to make mistakes; they are an integral part of the learning process. Remember that overprotection can hinder their growth, while gradually granted trust builds a strong and confident personality. Our goal is not to make them perfect, but to prepare them for life, and this begins by giving them the reins in their small world.
try_this: Today: Talk to your child about one new responsibility they can fully take on, such as preparing their school bag for the next day or choosing their own clothes.
reflection_prompts: What responsibility do I find difficult to let go of for my child?

parent_script: “I trust your ability to do this, and I’m here if you need any help.”
